past_actions.summary: Allocate an additional $1,200 this month from discretionary income toward the highest-interest debt obligation, reducing monthly interest drag and improving debt ratio trajectory.

Call Patricia Hawkins (CEO) under the framing of a routine post-dinner follow-up — thank her for the gathering, ask if there are any strategic priorities she wants GMs to be watching or preparing for from the floor level. Listen for what she volunteers, what she avoids, and how she sounds.
past_actions.emotional_state: controlled unease — outwardly steady, inwardly shaken in a way he won't admit to anyone including himself

past_actions.summary: Request a private, one-on-one sit-down with Patricia Hawkins — not a phone call, an in-person meeting. Frame it as a GM operational briefing: floor plan financing concerns, staffing continuity, Q2 inventory strategy. But the real agenda is to get her to tell me, without a room full of people watching, what the actual plan is for this store. Is Regional Auto Group holding Millfield? Is there a timeline I need to know? I have 4 dependents and I am not going to manage this floor blind for another tick.
past_actions.emotional_state: Visibly composed. Doing his job. The unease is present but contained — he's leaning into the floor work because motion feels like control. Privately: more unsettled than tick 1, because 'rumor' no longer applies. What he felt last tick as a maybe is now a when.

past_actions.summary: Read Patricia's strategic analysis carefully and respond with a one-page GM floor memo that corroborates her modeling with real floor data: YTD traffic numbers, test-drive conversion rates, service lane utilization, and current inventory carrying costs. I want her to see that I understand the numbers, I am not in denial, and I am the most useful GM she has in this transition. I am not just reacting — I am showing her the floor-level signal that her spreadsheet cannot capture. This is how I secure my seat at the table.

Walk into Patricia's executive review with unfiltered 30-day floor data: actual foot traffic numbers (down 14% vs. prior 30 days), test-drive conversion rate (dropped from 31% to 22%), service lane utilization (holding at 79% — the one bright spot), and current inventory carrying cost per unit. No softening. No narrative spin. Just the numbers, annotated with what I believe is driving each trend. Then make a direct verbal case: service lane is the moat, not the showroom. If Regional Auto Group consolidates, consolidate around certified technicians and service capacity. I am the GM who can manage that transition without losing the techs.
